chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Al-Yaqubi, from Isa ibn Abdullah, from Ali ibn Ja'far, who said:

Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) used to sniff Al-Shaleetha (a perfume) and the lily in intense heat, causing his nostrils to drop (moisture). He said: And Al-Reza (peace be upon him) also used to sniff with it. So I said to Ali ibn Ja'far, 'Why is that?' So Ali said, 'I mentioned that to one of the physicians, so he mentioned that it is good for copulation.'

key_terms.الشَّلِيثَا: A type of perfume or scent

ai.seo_question: What was the reason for the Imams sniffing lily or specific perfumes according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical medical knowledge of the Imams, specifically Imam Musa al-Kazim and Imam Ali al-Rida, who utilized lily oil (Shalitha) for its aphrodisiac properties as confirmed by contemporary physicians. It illustrates the Shia tradition of integrating spiritual authority with empirical health practices, demonstrating that the Imams engaged in daily life with both religious piety and scientific awareness. The reference to 'Shalitha' and 'Zanbaq' underscores the continuity of traditional herbal medicine within the Shia scholarly heritage.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Al Yaqouby, from Isa Bin Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassan Musaasws used to sniff Al-Shaleysa (a perfume), and the lily in intense heat, (until it) dropped (drops from hisasws nose), and Al-Rezaasws as well sniffed with it’. So I said to Ali son of Ja’farasws, ‘Why is that?’ So Ali said, ‘I mentioned that to one of the physicians, so he mentioned that it is very good for the copulation’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-‘ Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from al-Ya‘qubiy from ‘Isa ibn ‘Abd Allah from Ali ibn Ja‘far who has said the following:

“Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would smell al-Shalisha (a certain mixture) and gladiola as medicine to cure the heat of his runny nose. I asked ‘Ali ibn Ja‘far about it. Ali said that I mentioned it to a certain physician who said that it is very good for going to bed with one’s wife.’”
